name: Rubber Hose Animation
visualIdentity: Normalized from a Cuphead-inspired reference, not a named source style. Rounded figures, flexible tube-like limbs, bold silhouettes and expressive poses; preserve character identity with deliberate arcs, pivots and squash-and-stretch. Suggested new-art palette: vintage black silhouettes on warm off-white.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to illustrated mascots, character gags, retro brand stories, music videos, jingles, episodic shorts, and explainers with expressive characters. Inferred suitability: interactive HTML can use a deterministic loop with play/pause and static reduced-motion pose.
limitations: Avoid arbitrary limb deformation and identical bounces across objects. Omit or adapt gaze tracking if eyes, layers or a suitable rig are absent, movement distorts anatomy, or the character distracts. Do not imply that movement can alter actual footage without suitable asset production. Keep cards brief; avoid color inks, character letterpress texture and long text cards.
palette: Suggested only when no task, brand, approved source or existing semantic palette applies: background #F4ECD9, foreground #1C1B18; two monochrome tokens, no gradients or accent hues. Preserve supplied colors, role assignments, assets and style color limits. Use hatching, patterns or opacity for tone. The opaque pair’s stated contrast is 14.636:1, but check actual composited frames; this is not a full accessibility guarantee.
motionAndInteraction: Use anticipation, arcs, rhythmic poses and clear reactions; beat-keyed poses may land on beats with anticipation off-beat, without bouncing every object. Optional pointer gaze is bounded to eye sockets, returns neutrally, and is character animation, not viewer tracking. Interactive HTML may map pointer or finite scroll to deterministic states; support backward/direct seeking and reduced motion. Video uses authored composition time, never live input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Suggest music, voiceover, sung vocals, effects, ambience or silence to fit topic and user requirements; preserve speech clarity and synchronize accents with action. Music can support beat-locked poses, but audio is not required to understand content.
assetRequirements: Build characters from curved paths and replaceable poses using Canvas 2D or SVG; optional PixiJS can composite 2D sprites. Gaze needs suitable facial layers or a rig. Optional letterpress intertitles use the same black-and-cream palette and fixed grid. Use authorized audio/assets; availability is unspecified.
combinations: Style alone suits character gags. Optional style-105 adds beat timing for music, jingles or mascot loops, retaining the two-color palette and varied rhythms. Optional style-052 adds separate letterpress title cards between scenes; preserve palette, use cuts or iris transitions, and keep copy short. Combinations are suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: Choose drawing and motion methods for style fidelity first; one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is primary for composition, seekable timing, media/audio sync, validation and export. Use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, and record why; an existing React project alone is insufficient. Keep rendering and motion separate from export; deterministic time, seeded randomness and cached/baked state support seeking. Inspect representative frames and full video. Interactive input is HTML-only.
